subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU swarm rebalance and provisional hold request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU swarm rebalance and provisional hold request

Team —

We're at the late-stage negotiation for Aurelius Systems (DL-2026-1789). They want a dedicated footprint that effectively guarantees steady throughput for a high-concurrency inference tier starting mid-June. Sales has asked for a provisional hold while the contract language is finalized.

Can you do an availability check for 24 GPU-equivalents (baseline: 24xA100-80GB logical capacity) for a 90-day provisional hold window (target start 2026-06-15)? If strict A100s aren't available, propose a mixed mapping (A100/H100) with expected perf deltas. Key asks from Sales/Customer:
- Peak concurrent requests: approx 1.2k concurrent model workers
- Typical request size: median 1.5k tokens, bursty up to 10k tokens
- Tail latency SLO target: 95th < 300ms for the primary model

Please include:
- Fleet inventory snapshot (which clusters/nodes we would earmark)
- Impact to other late-stage deals if we reserve these units (known collisions)
- Any operational caveats (re-quantization required, cold-start implications)

I've attached a draft sizing worksheet (capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) with Sales' numbers. This is a provisional ask — do not commit to any SLA yet without Legal/Infra sign-off.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU swarm rebalance and provisional hold request

Karthik —

Quick inventory snapshot (high level):
- Available A100-80GB logical equivalents in our US pools for 2026-06: ~14 units (contingent)
- Available H100 physical units that can be provisioned as high-throughput alternatives: 30 nodes (would need runtime tuning)
- Cold spare capacity across regions that can be pulled in with 72h lead: ~10 units

Options to meet 24-equivalent ask:
1) Mix (preferred): 14xA100 + 10xH100 with a transparent routing policy. Expect ~+15-25% per-token perf on H100 side but slightly different latency profile. We can present a single endpoint + behind-the-scenes weighted routing.
2) Full H100 mapping: allocate 24 H100s and apply quantized model to match memory footprint; requires model retuning and a 2–3 week validation window.
3) Soft hold (non-exclusive): earmark nodes and implement higher-priority queueing for Aurelius; doesn't block other sales but reduces preemption risk.

Operational notes:
- If we mix hardware, we must version pin the model builds per node type and add an autosplitter in the load balancer. That increases rollout complexity and will need a dedicated release window.
- Impact: I see potential overlap with a HelioApps commit in the same week (probable conflict for A100 pool). If we choose option 1, we can minimize disruption by migrating HelioApps to H100s where feasible.

I'm attaching the fleet map for the US region — highlights the clusters I recommend holding.

Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: fleet_map_v2.xlsx (excel)]

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurelius.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU swarm rebalance and provisional hold request

Karthik / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick reply, Marcus — helpful context. A couple of clarifications from our side that will influence the hold we need: 
- Traffic profile: our initial estimates assume heavy multi-tenant traffic (50% p99-size bursts) as we onboard multiple internal teams. We can provide sample traces to help with profiling.
- Can you confirm whether the mixed A100/H100 mapping will present a single endpoint SLA? We prefer a deterministic latency band rather than a best-effort mapping.

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
1) Provisional 21-day hold starting June 15 while we finalize SLA language (we're comfortable shortening the window if Redwood needs it).
2) Run a 48-hour performance soak (customer-managed traffic) on the mixed mapping with agreed test prompts.
3) Contract signature to convert provisional hold to reserved capacity within 21 days of a successful soak.

We can do a brief call tomorrow to align on acceptance tests.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurelius Systems

[Aurelius Systems attachment: prod_traces_example.json (referenced)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@aurelius.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU swarm rebalance and provisional hold request

Elena / Team —

Appreciate the clear plan. Per infra notes above, here's what Redwood can commit to immediately (provisional, contingent on Legal/Infra sign-offs):
- Provisional 21-day non-exclusive hold (2026-06-15 to 2026-07-06) for up to 24 logical A100-equivalents. We'll implement option 1: mixed A100/H100 mapping with routing to keep endpoint surface stable.
- We will schedule the 48-hour performance soak during the hold window; Redwood will provide an acceptance test doc with traffic shape and expected telemetry.
- Expected blockers: final SLA language for latency tails and a runbook for cross-hardware consistency. I'll loop in Legal and Platform Ops for the SLA exception.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: can you coordinate Legal intake and draft the provisional hold amendment?
- Marcus: please lock the cluster candidates and add comments to JIRA-INF-4521 with the node IDs. Attach fleet_map_v2.xlsx updates there.
- Elena: please share the trace samples and a short list of acceptance prompts; we'll use those for the soak.

I'll set a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow at 10:30 PT — invite to follow. If anybody is unavailable, reply with an alternative.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
